extracted.intended_audience: educational administrators and school leaders seeking external grant funding
extracted.subtask_description: A practical guide for school leaders on the full grant lifecycle: surveying the funding landscape, forming proposal teams, structuring and writing competitive proposals, planning evaluation, submitting, and post-submission follow-up. Tailored to educational contexts and equity-driven improvement projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the current grant landscape
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine the current grant landscape to know what funding opportunities exist and how they are changing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper 'examines the current grant landscape' — administrators should be aware of trends, major funders, and funding priorities to target proposals effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorize available funding types
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorize funding by type (e.g., federal grants, private foundations, competitive vs. formula funding) to match projects with suitable sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide 'categorizes available funding types' so applicants can select appropriate mechanisms and tailor strategy to each funder type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify potential funding sources strategically
rubrics_metrics.description: Use deliberate strategies to identify potential funders whose priorities align with the school's needs and project goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper 'provides strategies for identifying potential funding sources' — implies systematic searches, leveraging networks, and aligning project aims with funder interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build collaborative proposal teams
rubrics_metrics.description: Form and manage collaborative teams to develop proposals, bringing together complementary skills and stakeholder buy-in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis is placed on 'building collaborative proposal teams' — guidance includes assembling diverse expertise, clarifying roles, and ensuring stakeholder engagement in design and implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow structural components of grant proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand and include the standard structural components required in proposals (e.g., needs statement, goals/objectives, methods, budget, timeline, sustainability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide stresses 'understanding the structural components of grant proposals' so submissions meet funder formatting and content expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write with clarity and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Write proposal text clearly, concisely, and purposefully to communicate need, planned activities, and anticipated outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper emphasizes 'writing with clarity and purpose' — good proposals are readable, directly tied to evidence and goals, and avoid jargon or vague language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include evaluation planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a clear evaluation plan describing how project outcomes will be measured and how data will be used for improvement and accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide 'addresses evaluation planning' — applicants should specify metrics, data-collection methods, baseline and targets, and responsible parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the submission process carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere strictly to submission procedures, deadlines, required formats, and application checklists to avoid disqualification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper covers 'the submission process' — implies compliance with funder instructions, uploading documents correctly, and meeting timeline constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use effective post-submission strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ post-submission actions such as follow-up communications, readiness to provide clarifications, and planning for award management and stewardship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide discusses 'effective post-submission strategies' — including monitoring outcomes of review, responding to funder requests, and preparing for implementation if funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align proposals with educational excellence and equity
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame proposals to demonstrate how funding will promote educational improvement, innovation, and equity within the school context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper's aim is to 'empower leaders to leverage grant funding in pursuit of educational excellence and equity' — proposals should make explicit connections to student outcomes and equitable impacts.
